# Per-node MCP servers, bounded by an operator allowlist

A node declares the MCP servers its agent may reach. The operator declares which
servers any node may name. The agent gets the intersection, plus the executor's
own callback server.

## The template

Three agent nodes, each declaring a different single inline server.

```yaml
name: mcp-per-node-demo
version: "1"
nodes:
  - type: alpha
    executor: claude-agent
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          model:         {type: string, default: "claude-sonnet-4-5"}
          system_prompt: {type: string, default: "per-node MCP"}
          user_prompt:   {type: string, default: "..."}
          cli:
            type: object
            default:
              mcp_servers:
                - transport: http
                  name: validator
                  url: "http://validator:9/mcp/validator"

  - type: beta
    executor: claude-agent
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          model:         {type: string, default: "claude-sonnet-4-5"}
          system_prompt: {type: string, default: "per-node MCP"}
          user_prompt:   {type: string, default: "..."}
          cli:
            type: object
            default:
              mcp_servers:
                - transport: http
                  name: local-tool
                  url: "http://local-tool:9/mcp/local-tool"

  - type: gamma
    executor: claude-agent
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          model:         {type: string, default: "claude-sonnet-4-5"}
          system_prompt: {type: string, default: "per-node MCP"}
          user_prompt:   {type: string, default: "..."}
          cli:
            type: object
            default:
              mcp_servers:
                - transport: http
                  name: forbidden-tool
                  url: "http://forbidden-tool:9/mcp/forbidden-tool"
```

MCP servers are inline-only. `transport` is `http`, `stdio`, or `module`
(`http-loopback` is an alias for `module`).

## With an operator allowlist in force

```bash
docker run -d -p 8080:8080 \
  -e CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=... \
  -e RIMSKY_CLAUDE_AGENT_MCP_ALLOWLIST=validator,local-tool \
  rimsky-all-in-one:<tag>
```

`alpha`'s agent is handed exactly `validator` plus `rimsky-callback`, the
executor's own server. `beta`'s agent is handed exactly `local-tool` plus
`rimsky-callback`. Neither sees the other's server.

`gamma` names a server outside the allowlist. Its dispatch fails with
`agent/attribute_invalid`, and the error payload names the server
(`disallowed_mcp_server: forbidden-tool`), the instance, the node, and the
allowlist variable `RIMSKY_CLAUDE_AGENT_MCP_ALLOWLIST`.

A template author cannot widen the operator's boundary by declaring a server.

## With no operator allowlist

Run the same template with `RIMSKY_CLAUDE_AGENT_MCP_ALLOWLIST` unset.

`gamma` now runs and its agent sees `forbidden-tool` plus `rimsky-callback`.
`alpha` and `beta` still see only their own declarations. Removing the
operator's boundary does not merge the nodes' tool surfaces: what a node's agent
may reach is still what that node declared.
